record_notes.DCP-LETT-1063: February 26, 1847, Down address but actual Shrewsbury location per apparatus. Missing August 30 Muñiz letter/papers arrived recently after delay with unidentified Morris, expressly not John Morris. Earlier 1061 already attests possession February 12; do not shift arrival forward to this acknowledgment. Sale conditions newly understood, agent shipment suggested, translation/publication attempted prospectively, Muñi-felis identity suspected. Conditional South America gift depends on English ability and channel, scarlet-fever pamphlet donation planned. Earlier Niata information via Lumb known but original not preserved; domestic/feral animal questions unanswered. Owen Paris-arrival news is a report, not direct inspection.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1241A: Authentic excerpt quoted in Murchison paper read May 30, 1849, from a recent letter; full letter absent. Raw before-May-30 range has artificial 1809 lower bound, Malvern location supplied but no exact day. Darwin says glacier and floating-ice effects indistinguishable in many cases at present, not all cases forever. Murchison use of quotation is separate from Darwin observed Welsh evidence and does not establish missing incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1060: February 10, supplied 1847, request through bearer for February Geological Journal and any parcels, with twelve shillings enclosed. Nichols or alternate Charlton routing not receipt/read proof. Desire for Sharpe paper is editorial likelihood; no actual delivery date or source-complete prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1143: Copy, Tuesday evening in supplied 1848 with no exact day. Thanks missing Norman note, reports servant consultation with Latter contradicting assumed affidavit procedure. Earlier Snow/Scott episode recalled, Scott travel now conjectured. Servant sent to Maidstone because three special jury cases too much strain; excusal is editorial probability from missing travel record, not demonstrated outcome. Historical court procedure is source context, not present legal guidance.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1304: Council minute item 5 dated February 22, 1850, describing missing Darwin offer of British fossil cirripede monograph. Authentic institutional record readable, Darwin letter text absent. Acceptance and supervisory appointments in minutes are council acts, not proved Darwin knowledge or exact offer composition. Raw before-February-22 date does not identify a day or create Darwin voice.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1353: September 10, supplied 1850. Four or five woodcuts wanted, drawings on wood commissioned/made, permission to cut and allocation of costs still queried. Proposes Latin and English descriptions and asks approval; later books with both languages are not current approval. Prior June translation and August correction payments in apparatus can coexist with request, do not move final format decision earlier. Bowerbank person and society routing retained; annual-volume binding criticism is personal preference, not implemented change.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1081: April 17, supplied 1847 from printed brackets. March 9 note and book received yesterday, April 16 under assigned year, after waiting uncollected at Geological Society. Praises condensed information and woodcuts but no explicit complete reading statement. Education commissioners adoption heard; future naturalists hoped. Note itself absent, no direct pair.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1289: Fresh full available Pickering memorandum, Boston January 9, 1850. Journal copied from weeks after September 1839 Metia visit, specimens not in hand. Raw HTML contains six prose blocks only, no 73-species list; ten bis marks known only through editorial description. Final reassessment says non-maritime remainder nearly all introduced, retaining qualification. Already accepted knowledge edge to 1305 by February 24, actual receipt unknown; no direct prompt or new edge counted. Dana routing editorial inference and missing cover preserved.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1114: September 7, conjectured 1848 and probable Quekett recipient. Bottle search based on imperfect Sowerby/Darwin recollection of earlier loan to Owen; cannot prove present location. Square green or round white bottles, coarse restored rags, tin numbered tags described; tiny tag figure visually read, no legible serial number. October visit planned. First Scalpellum larva muscles show no visible striae at best power, second-stage striae visible; later embryonic voluntary-movement knowledge must not overwrite observation. Year rationale uses lack of later travel plans, not exact independent proof.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1223F: Incomplete quoted Reeve testimonial, known received by Reeve on March 14, 1849 according to diary. That is recipient receipt, not Darwin incoming knowledge or exact composition; raw open lower bound retained. Hears of Reeve zeal and intends signature for Royal Society candidature; actual signature/election not established here, later failure separate. Missing application request remains missing.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1329: May 20, supplied 1850. Circular just received, quotes free-journal offer and requests missing numbers since last 1845 volume to Athenaeum. Quoted sentence does not recover whole circular, request does not prove delivery/read. Last received volume year is not exact last delivery date. Secretary identity not named.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1121: Complete surviving eleven-page autograph draft represented as one long body paragraph. After September 20, 1847, raw latest September 30; never published in Scotsman according to later witness. Main source is Milne private memoir, Lyell discussion and own field memory, not preserved incoming editor question. Rejects detrital barriers, evaluates glacier-lake advantages and objections, still inclines to marine theory with conditional ice-lake alternative if wrong. Numbered objections and research questions, skipped numbering and literal draft repetitions retained; no deletion/addition markup to justify silent cleanup. Literal 212 vertical feet is not MathML two-and-a-half. Proposed measurements/observations are future enquiries. Quoted/glossed source references remain separate from author text.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1369F: October 11, supplied 1850. Sent for parcels yesterday, Sedgwick fifth edition received this morning; first edition read earlier at unknown date, new expanded book only planned reading for school choice. November 12 reading log is later. Darwin calls son eleven although birthday still ahead; preserve original wording with separate correction, no redating. Water-cure improvement and permanent-stomach expectation are his historical health beliefs. Missing cover note and future Rugby schooling not current input/result.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-116: Fresh complete September 4, 1831 Sedgwick context and figure. Darwin note delayed by waiter until hours before September 2 departure, so field visit August 31 predates seeing it. Answers missing Cwm Idwal/Moel Shabod note, distinguishes fossils and trap/slate ordering and admits diagram out of proportion. Daily August 21–September 4 itinerary is reported history, subsequent traverse forecast. Lithology in postscript uncertain identification and possibly different spot. No connection to 1850 Discourse gift.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-129: Fresh complete September 18, 1831 Sedgwick context with labelled geological cross-section and table legend. Assumes earlier letter 116 received, not proof of Darwin receipt. Congratulates appointment, recommends books and Lonsdale, proposes Society nomination not actual 1836 election. Geological axis expected next year, present observations limited. Manuscript legend includes h while preserved figure ends k; retain figure/legend mismatch without inventing label. Later field synthesis and book annotations not present-day receipt evidence.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-459: Fresh December 21, supplied 1838. Reports Geological Society council unwilling to recommend Jukes corporately, but well wishes and possible individual recommendations from Sedgwick/Whewell. Darwin assistance offered, Greenough limited acquaintance noted. Missing Jukes application and Sedgwick communication cannot be recovered from account. No 1850 Sedgwick book prompt.

record_notes.DCP-LETT-1372: Accepted full primary reading reused with matching hashes. Fresh complete extra reading: November 26, supplied 1850. Encloses account cheque and agrees with Salt view that five thousand of Owen loan is personal, a contemporary belief later corrected. Emma inheritance said already invested by trustees; proposes share transfer only if advantages exceed costs and asks Salt decision. Missing Salt incoming letter not reproduced. Later August 1851 exchange and 1853 correction in apparatus must not condition November 1850 belief. Footnote mortgage interest MathML is three and three quarters percent, editorial layer, not flattened 334 or current quoted letter prose.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1061: Accepted full primary reading reused with matching hashes. February 12 with supplied 1847 year. Received Muñiz letter and papers after almost four months lying in London, not four months in Darwin possession. Offers fossils through College; Darwin initially understands gift rather than sale, asks missing Megatherium parts list, shipping expenses, publications and encouragement. Machairodus identity is his hypothesis, later Smilodon classification editorial. Spanish newspaper paper has arrived, English translation still planned; asks Paris shipment news. Owen fish lectures first chapter read, not all chapters until later March record. Acasta application declined because fresh British specimens obtained. Missing Muñiz letter and Owen suggestion cannot be recreated; later 1063 identifies the August 30 input but is another outgoing witness. Museum minute summary of purchase is not sufficient to override later uncompleted negotiation evidence.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1305: Accepted full primary reading reused with matching hashes. February 24, supplied 1850. Future Wednesday dispatch of delayed papers/specimens; Bell delay and Westwood bereavement. Thanks missing Dana answers, Gould/Dana specimens, notice of geological review, and explicitly Pickering for Pacific plant list. Pickering 1289 is a distinct surviving knowledge source. Distinguishes knowledge of review from actually reading it. Explains hypothesized cement duct as modified ovarian branch and Goodsir parasite correction, reports observed sexual arrangements and asks fossil record; preserve contemporary error rather than substitute later gland correction. Goodsir presumed lost but expedition fate unknown. Lyell article remains future publication. Specimen gratitude alone does not fix physical arrival day.
